newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia privatises three more state companies.
newsitem.headline: Zambia privatises three more state companies.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Thursday it had privatised three more state-run enterprises.
The government has sold 197 of its 326 companies since it launched an ambitious privatisation programme in 1993.

Announcing the sale of Kawmabwa Tea Company, Kafironda Ltd and the Lusaka Engineering Company, ZPA chief Valentine Chitalu said negotiations for the sale of another seven companies had been completed.

The heads of agreement for one other company had also been finalised and a further 26 companies were ready for privatisation. The sale of eight more companies was being held up by legal action and receiverships, he said.
The ZPA chief said commercial explosives and accessories company Kafironda Ltd had been sold to ICI Explosives (Africa) Ltd, a principle shareholder in Covilink and Cobar.
"Thirty-four percent shares in Kafironda held by the government were offered to Covilink and Cobar who waived their (pre-emptive) rights in favour of ICI Explosives," Chitalu said.

"Government shares in Kafironda were sold for a price consideration of $783,902 and full consideration has been paid. ICI has also allowed ZPA to float 20 percent shares to the public in the future," he added.
Kawambwa Tea Company was sold to Metal Distributors (UK) and Hemant Jalan for 4.66 billion kwacha.
Amanita Zambiana Ltd acquired 60 percent shares in Zambia's leading metal and fabrication engineering business, Engineering Company Ltd (Lenco), for 1.8 billion kwacha.

"The other 40 percent shares are held by Piacenza and Intersomer of Italy who each hold 20 percent. It is ZPA's understanding that Amanita is expected to complete negotiations with the minority shareholders to acquire their 40 percent stake," Chitalu said. ($=1,228 kwacha)
